title: Why Los Angeles City Hall is Under Federal Investigation
seoTitle: Why LA City Hall is Under Federal Investigation
subtitle: House Subcommittee Letter Demands Mayor Karen Bass's Testimony on LAHSA
excerpt: A Congressional subcommittee sent a letter to the Los Angeles mayor requesting testimony on alleged waste, fraud, and mismanagement of allocated federal funds.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Los Angeles City Hall has come under national scrutiny after a House of Representatives subcommittee sent a letter to Mayor Karen Bass requesting her testimony at a hearing on alleged waste and fraud in federal funds earmarked for combating homelessness.

What Prompted the Summons to Capitol Hill

The Subcommittee on Government Efficiency, led by Representative Tim Burchett, expressed concern over the possible misallocation of federal dollars by the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA). The letter mentions reports of "flagrant corruption" in LAHSA's contracting processes and highlights an increase in the homeless population during Bass's tenure.

Municipal Administration's Reactions

The mayor's attorney, David Michaelson, responded that the administration would not make Bass available for testimony and disputed the allegations, pointing to an 11% drop in unsheltered homeless individuals since 2022. Michaelson also reported that the city is preparing a plan for Los Angeles to directly manage homeless services, reducing reliance on LAHSA.

LAHSA's Stance

The agency stated that it welcomes external audits and evaluations to improve its work and that no review has found evidence of fraud or corruption. In response to the letter, LAHSA reiterated its commitment to transparency and the effectiveness of assistance programs.

Legal and Financial Context

In June, the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) suspended LAHSA from requesting and spending federal funds, citing mismanagement. The suspension prevented the agency from submitting a $240 million request planned for August 26. LAHSA filed a lawsuit against HUD, and a federal judge granted a preliminary injunction, deeming the suspension "arbitrary and capricious" and potentially harmful to the public interest.

Political Implications

The summons comes as Bass faces a tough electoral contest against Councilmember Nithya Raman, who criticizes the handling of the homelessness crisis. The debate over "Housing First" and "Harm Reduction" policies has also been central to discussions, with Representative Burchett questioning their effectiveness.

With information from Los Angeles Times, LAist.
